solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tongue rotten, put away

parts.note: a tongue is a language, here the language of Poland
food gone rotten is said to be off

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a spoiled ox tongue before storing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like meat to go with 'rotten', but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To put food away is to eat it all up, an informal idiom for finishing a meal.

clue.text: Kiss Hollywood great

definitions.meaning: a quick light kiss on the cheek
Gregory ..., star of To Kill a Mockingbird

explanation.surface: A screen legend's famous kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a brief kiss; the other is the surname of the film star Gregory Peck.

clue.text: Hide face finally in bubbles

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter inside the word for bubbles

parts.note: a lather is a mass of soapy bubbles

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word face

explanation.surface: Someone hides their face at last under a mass of soap suds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, and tanned skin is the material used for shoes and belts.

clue.text: Long blade in swordsman's kit

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words swordsman's kit

explanation.surface: A fencer's equipment includes a long sword blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Long blade' a sword, but it is a runner for snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Each runner strapped to a skier's boot is a long narrow blade for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Chemical in petroleum at once exploding

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters of at once apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A volatile chemical in petrol suddenly blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: This hydrocarbon is a component of petrol, used to rate its resistance to engine knocking.

clue.text: In European country, history ignores Tory voting privilege

indicators.note: In places what follows inside the name of the country

parts.note: France is a country in Europe

indicators.note: ignores tells us to leave the letters of Tory out of history

explanation.surface: In France, the record of the past pays no heed to a Conservative's right to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' leaves HIS, from which 'In' puts inside the country. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote in elections, a formal term for suffrage.

clue.text: River appeared without end

indicators.note: without end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: someone who appeared came along

explanation.surface: A river showed up and never stopped flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the English river running past the Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Job centre welcoming husband

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest inside, so the abbreviation goes within

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A Jobcentre receptionist greets a married man looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a British government employment office; the clue splits the word so 'Job' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a routine task, especially a tedious domestic one.

clue.text: Country where chap admits felony ultimately hurt

indicators.note: admits means letting something in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of felony

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: A man confesses that a crime finally caused harm somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar is the Southeast Asian nation formerly called Burma.

clue.text: Old racer having discussion about former Olympic hosts

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chat goes round the host city

parts.note: a chat is an informal discussion
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics

explanation.surface: An old athlete talks about cities that once staged the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old racer' suggests a retired runner, but it is a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome and Greece, horse-drawn two-wheeled carts were raced in arenas.

clue.text: Almost everyone I see gets a greeting

indicators.note: almost means not quite whole, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone means all
oh is the exclamation of someone who says I see

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody I meet says hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used both for hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Shriek getting cuts — might this foam have helped?

indicators.note: cuts means slicing into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a scream is a shriek
getting something is having it

explanation.surface: A man yelps as he nicks himself; a better lather might have spared him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as nicks from a razor, but it signals one word slicing into the other. The definition ties back to the surface, so the clue is close to an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The lather applied before using a razor softens stubble and helps prevent nicks.

clue.text: Venetian lover's first, tragic sweetheart

indicators.note: tragic suggests something ruined, so the letters are mixed into a new order
first picks out the opening letter of lover's

explanation.surface: A Venetian's first love ended in tragedy, as in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is someone chosen as a love on 14 February, hence a sweetheart.

clue.text: Creative skill in work, to some extent

indicators.note: in places the creative skill inside the word for work

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
art is creative skill

explanation.surface: Artistry in a job only counts for so much.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means in part, not entirely.

clue.text: Drop fruit on me, last one in basket

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: last one in picks out the final letter of basket

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a fruit to be dropped on them, the final one in the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, as a stone does.

clue.text: Good to enter better digit

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so the letter sits within the word

parts.note: finer means better

explanation.surface: A good number is needed to get into a better position.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a finger or toe, the anatomical sense of the word.

clue.text: Something syrupy to drop in explosive device

indicators.note: to drop means letting the following word fall out

parts.note: grenadine is a sweet red pomegranate syrup

explanation.surface: A sticky substance is about to fall into a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand.

clue.text: Found upside down in field, dirty puzzle

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the letters read from bottom to top
Found tells us the letters are discovered inside the words that follow
in confirms the letters lie within field, dirty

explanation.surface: A grubby conundrum turns up the wrong way round in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question with a clever answer, like a conundrum.

clue.text: Nice and sound after treatment, scarlet rash

indicators.note: after treatment means the letters have been worked on and changed in order

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A doctor in Nice treats a patient for a red skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like the skin complaint in the medical surface, but it is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe action taken without thought, so careless and hasty.

clue.text: Top money once

definitions.meaning: the top of the head, or the highest part of a hill
a former British coin worth five shillings

explanation.surface: The top coin of a bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: It means the summit of the head and also an old British coin worth a quarter of a pound.

clue.text: Irish working for club

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: An Irishman labours at a golf or social club.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, an iron is a club with a metal head used for shorter shots.

clue.text: I wander back to see Antipodean people

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A traveller returns to visit people in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: Antipodean refers to Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Misery caused by spinning of a spider

indicators.note: spinning of whirls the letters of a spider into a new order

explanation.surface: Arachnophobia: someone is upset by a spider spinning its web.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is a state of utter hopelessness, a deep wretchedness.

clue.text: Hang rabbit up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rabbit or to gas both mean to chatter on at length

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang a dead rabbit up, as in a butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like an animal; it is British slang for talk, as is 'gas'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or hang down loosely.

clue.text: Container idiot knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a nit is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool knocks over a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for food or other goods.

clue.text: Enduring horrible revenge, sovereign incarcerated

indicators.note: incarcerated means locked up inside, so the royal letters go within
horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A terrible act of vengeance lands a monarch in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' shuffles the fodder to EVGREEN, and 'incarcerated' puts the royal cipher inside it, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen stays fresh and popular over time, like a tree keeping its leaves.
